answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity forge a single unbroken chain of useful work: before an agent may trade, it must complete small jobs whose outputs are checked by strangers, and each check adds one link that cannot be parallelised. Picture a workshop lit by an umber lamp, where the pulse of honest activity is measured over weeks, not minutes. A thousand fakes would each need a thousand real chains, so flooding the market costs more than it earns.
